title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness, starvation prevention, and timeouts
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: We observed intermittent starvation of low-priority long-tail requests and head-of-line blocking under high-concurrency workloads in the continuous batcher. This PR tunes the scheduler to improve queueing fairness, add starvation prevention heuristics, and introduce conservative timeouts to bound latency for stuck batches. Changes are intentionally opt-in via config flags so we can canary safely.

Summary of changes: implemented a per-priority credit allocator (token-bucket style) to ensure progress for lower-priority queues; added max_wait and max_pending_timeouts for in-flight batches to detect and flush stuck batches; improved queue sampling to favor starving queues; exposed new metrics (batcher.queue_wait_seconds_bucket, batcher.starvation_evictions, batcher.flush_timeouts) and tracing spans for schedule decisions; small kernel-selection guard to avoid switching kernels during stalled KV cache warmup.

Why this approach: a token/credit allocator prevents a single high-throughput priority from monopolizing batch slots; explicit timeouts bound how long a request can be held waiting for a batch which fixes pathological head-of-line cases; metrics and tracing let us validate behavior in production and rollback quickly if needed.

Testing & perf: unit and integration tests added to cover fairness logic and timeout behavior. Local perf runs on p3/rtx configs show: p50 generation latency ~+/-0% (unchanged), p95 latency down ~12% under mixed workloads, sustained throughput up ~6% due to fewer stalled batches, and observable reduction in starvation_evictions after tuning. Full perf harness runs were executed in CI.

Rollout plan: 1) merge behind feature flag default=false; 2) enable for 5% of traffic in canary; 3) monitor batcher.* metrics and p95 latency; 4) expand to 25%/50%/100% if stable. Safeguards: automatic rollback policy on perf-regression or spike in flush_timeouts.

Checklist:
- [x] Implementation with config toggles
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Perf harness runs and numbers in PR description
- [x] Metrics + tracing added
- [x] Docs/ops runbook updated

Related: ENG-3245 (continuous-batcher fairness), SUP-1298 (incidents related to KV cache warmup).

review_comments: Daniel Kim: Can you justify the default max_wait=250ms? It seems aggressive for long context workloads.
Aisha Patel: max_wait is conservative; it's configurable per-deploy and we set longer defaults for long-context models. Added a note in docs and made the default per-model configurable.

release_notes:
- Tuned continuous batcher scheduler: improved queueing fairness and starvation prevention; added conservative timeouts to bound head-of-line blocking.
- New metrics: batcher.queue_wait_seconds_bucket, batcher.starvation_evictions, batcher.flush_timeouts_count.
- Rollout behind feature flag with canary steps documented in docs/ops/continuous-batcher-tuning.md
notes: Measured improvements: p95 latency down ~12% in mixed-priority workloads; sustained throughput +6%; no regressions on p50. Feature gated for safe rollout.
testing_instructions: Run runtime/tests/test_scheduler.py and runtime/tests/integration/test_continuous_batcher.py. To reproduce perf runs use tools/perf/harness with --workload=mixed_priority and compare batcher.* metrics.
